title: Comparison of Buteyko Technique and Pursed Lip Breathing in Asthma
brief_summary: The objective of the study was to compare the effects of Buteyko breathing technique and pursed lip breathing technique in the management of asthma. A randomized controlled trial was conducted on 60 asthmatic patients randomly allocated to Buteyko technique group and pursed lip breathing group. Both the groups received 4 weeks of treatment, 3 times per week. Data was collected at base line, 2nd week and 4th week. Outcome measurements included FVC, FEV, PEFR and Asthma Control Test Questionnaire scores. Data analysis was carried out on Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) v.21.0. Confidence interval was kept at 95% and a p-value of less than 0.05 was considered significant.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients categorized as mild to moderate persistent asthma category according to the "National Asthma Education and Prevention Program"

Exclusion Criteria:

* Use of oral steroids within the four-week run-in period,
* Change in inhaled steroid dose and type,
* Other significant unstable medical conditions,
* They have undertaken Buteyko breathing technique previously.
